newsitem.title: USA: CBOT August soybeans limit-up on weather worries.
newsitem.headline: CBOT August soybeans limit-up on weather worries.

text.p: Concerns about dry weather in parts of the U.S. Midwest pushed August and September soybeans to limit gains at midsession Monday, traders said.
"The market is hypersensitive at this time of year," said one floor trader. "At this point, it's a weather scare, not a weather problem."
The rain that fell over the weekend was said to miss a large area of central Illinois where it is considered too dry, traders and forecasters said.
Additionally, forecasts show that much of the week will remain dry except for scattered rains, traders said.
The weather is not seen damaging the crop, but some sources report that soybeans, especially in central Illinois are shorter than normal and could use more moisture.

Traders shurgged off export shipment data that fell at the low end of expectations. The U.S. Department of Agriculture reported shipments of 4.716 million bushels. That figure was below expectations for five to eight million bushels.
In earlier trade, Prudential Securities bought six million bushels of August. The pool in August was two million bushels.
At 1114 CDT, August soybeans were 30 cents per bushel higher at $7.80, and other months were up 24 to 35-1/4 cents.
